html:
Severe knee pain can make daily life exhausting, but many elderly adults in Gujarat delay joint surgery because they also manage chronic conditions like high blood pressure (hypertension) or kidney disease. A question we hear daily is: Is knee replacement actually safe for me?

The response to that is yes, as long as your condition has been optimised medically prior to the operation. High blood pressure and problems with the kidneys do not necessarily mean that you cannot get a new knee, but it requires specific medical precautions.

If you are consulting a total knee replacement hospital in Ahmedabad, here is the exact information you need to know as a patient.

What High Blood Pressure Means for Knee Surgery

Uncontrolled hypertension increases the risk of excessive bleeding, sudden blood pressure drops under anesthesia, and cardiac stress.

  • Target Numbers: Surgeons and anesthesiologists generally require your blood pressure to be consistently below 160/100 mmHg in the weeks leading up to surgery. On the morning of surgery, a reading above 180/110 mmHg may cause a postponement to keep you safe.
  • Medication Adjustments: Most BP medications (like beta-blockers) are continued right up to the morning of surgery with a sip of water. However, your doctor may ask you to hold specific tablets, like ACE inhibitors or ARBs, on the day of surgery to prevent sharp blood pressure drops during anesthesia.

What Kidney Disease (CKD) Means for Joint Replacement

Kidneys detoxify the body and regulate medications. When it comes to patients with Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD), they run the risk of suffering from an overdose of fluids and medications during surgery.

  • Required Lab Markers: Your physician will look at your eGFR (estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate) and serum creatinine values. People who have mildly or moderately damaged kidneys (eGFR greater than 30-45 ml/min) can safely get a knee replacement with proper precautions.
  • Kidney-Safe Pain Relief: NSAIDs (anti-inflammatory painkillers), which are the usual analgesic drugs, such as ibuprofen and diclofenac, pose a great threat to damaged kidneys. After the operation, doctors use kidney-friendly analgesics, nerve blocks, and localised cooling methods.

Integrated Multi-Specialty Safety

At Silver Touch Hospitals, joint replacements for high-risk patients are performed under a co-managed protocol. Our Orthopaedic surgeons, Nephrologists, Cardiologists, and Critical Care team work together to monitor your fluid balance, kidney function, and blood pressure continuously through surgery and recovery.

Choosing an experienced total knee replacement hospital in Ahmedabad with dedicated ICU infrastructure ensures that your vital organs remain protected while you regain your pain-free mobility.
